minutes.headline: Committee declared TC Paso artifacts surplus for the Historical Society and approved a letter to the MSBA; FY25 cuts loom.
minutes.summary: The committee heard comment on town road closures that disrupted bus routes, declared old school artifacts surplus with first refusal to the Historical Society, accepted the Keystone report, and approved a revised letter to the MSBA. The superintendent presented class size, added-position and BCBA data for FY25 budget development, and members said cuts will have impact. The meeting ended with a motion to enter executive session.

public_comment.topic: Resident thanked the committee ahead of the vote on releasing TC Paso-era documents and described a scrapbook to go to the Historical Society.
Resident praised the craft fair held in the cafeteria by the soccer team.
Resident, speaking personally as a taxpayer, said the grant-funded positions were always cautioned to go away and hard decisions are coming.
Resident asked whether the health insurance stabilization account is depleted or still available.

votes.motion: Declare the items outlined in the memo surplus with intent to make them available to the Historical Society; unclaimed items taken up later.
Accept the Keystone educational collaborative annual report.
Approve the letter to the MSBA with adjustments.
Go into executive session at 7:55 p.m. to discuss collective bargaining strategy.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved a revised letter to the MSBA, with adjustments, by a passed vote.
The committee declared the TC Paso-era items in a memo surplus, with the Historical Society offered them first; unclaimed items were deferred.
The committee accepted the Keystone educational collaborative annual report by a passed vote.
The superintendent said current needs cannot fit in the usual annual increase for FY25, citing contractual bus costs and projected health insurance increases.
The committee agreed to wait for the incoming finance director before seeking outside MSBA guidance.

why_it_matters: The FY25 school budget is being framed as one where needs exceed the usual increase, so residents may be asked to weigh cuts or a larger school appropriation at budget time.
Two pressures were named on the record, the loss of grant-funded positions and a health insurance increase, and a budget line that rises for either reason looks the same on the page.
watch_next: The FY25 budget development discussion, where class size, added-position and BCBA data were presented as the basis for decisions on cuts.
